title: Elephant-Goldfish Model
by: Google's open-source plugin by Jim Quinn, Elise Ewing and Dave Rensin; its README says thousands of Google engineers use it. Read from its skills and reviewer prompts.
summary: Design with an elephant, review with a goldfish. A deep-context agent (the elephant) explores the idea with you and drafts the specification. Zero-context reviewers (goldfish) read only the document and what it links, so they expose unstated assumptions and blind spots. You resolve the trade-offs and approve the spec before any code is written, and the spec stays checked against the code for drift.

steps.name: Brainstorm
steps.writes: a concept brief, challenged by fresh reviewers

gates.what: You approve the design; it is then implemented in the normal workflow.

loops.when: drift: update the spec or the code

ideas: Elephant and goldfish: the agent with all the context drafts; agents with none of it review, because one thread that interviews, designs and codes ends up validating its own assumptions.
A goldfish reads only the document and what it links. If a fresh reader can't follow it, the document is missing context, and that can't be contested.
The paraphrase test: the reviewer first writes what the document proposes in its own words; the author compares it with the intent, and a wrong paraphrase is a finding.
Review lenses in order: zoom out (YAGNI, reuse of existing code found by searching, the root problem), comprehension, critic, zoom out again, implementation readiness.

Answering findings: fix, contest only with evidence the reviewer could read, escalate when the evidence is only in someone's head, decline a nit. "This was intentional" is not evidence, and the author's wish to contest is not either.

Convergence: settled findings stay settled, a fixed finding raised again re-opens, two consecutive clean rounds (no open Blocker or Major), a cap of five rounds, and churn when a new finding sits on a fix.
A reviewer that failed or returned nothing did not review: it is "not run", never zero findings.
Artifact first: long drafts and reports go to files, never into the chat.
No glazing: critique first; agreement has to be earned; no flattery and no apologies.
Living specifications: designs are checked in, and a drift report lists only where code and spec differ.
The skills are tested too: each has fixed test scenarios with expected behaviour.
